entries.title: Large IDs overflow JS safe integers
entries.body: JSON numbers beyond 2^53-1 lose precision in JavaScript. Return large DB/order IDs as strings (e.g. Twitter id_str). Schemas should use type:'string' with a pattern for such identifiers to stay exact.

entries.title: additionalProperties misses composed branches
entries.body: additionalProperties:false only sees directly-declared properties, not those contributed by allOf/anyOf/oneOf. Use unevaluatedProperties:false for strict closed objects when using composition.

entries.title: multipleOf has floating-point equality pitfalls
entries.body: multipleOf comparison uses floating-point math; edge cases like 0.1/0.3 can fail unexpectedly. Prefer integer-scaled values or tolerant epsilon checks where exact division matters.

entries.title: format:'email' is assertion-only when enabled
entries.body: Without ajv-formats / validateFormats, format:'email' is annotation-only and passes any string. Always enable format assertion for user-input validation to actually reject bad emails.

entries.title: nullable:true is only valid in OpenAPI 3.0 / draft-04
entries.body: nullable:true is an OpenAPI 3.0 / draft-04 concept and is invalid in JSON Schema 2020-12 or OpenAPI 3.1. Migrate to type:[...,'null'] to avoid silent validation gaps and broken schemas.

entries.title: date-time must be RFC 3339
entries.body: format:'date-time' expects RFC 3339 (e.g. 2024-01-01T00:00:00Z). Values like 2024/01/01 or 25:00:00 fail in full validation mode. Keep format assertion enabled to enforce it.

entries.title: if/then/else can make required conditional
entries.body: Use if/then/else to apply required only when a condition holds (e.g. require 'card' when 'type'=='credit'). Misuse of allOf + oneOf can produce confusing multi-error output for callers.

entries.title: pattern regex is ECMA-262; watch for backtracking
entries.body: pattern uses ECMA-262 regex semantics. Nested quantifiers on adversarial input can cause catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS). Anchor patterns and keep them simple to avoid denial-of-service.

entries.title: enum matches by deep equality, order-independent
entries.body: enum membership is by deep equality and order-independent; a single-element enum equals const. Complex nested enum values are valid but costly to compare at scale, so prefer flat enums.

entries.title: $ref resolution depends on $id base and loader
entries.body: Remote $ref requires the referenced schema to be added (addSchema/loadSchema) or fetched. Missing refs throw at compile time; circular refs are supported when properly $id-anchored.
